note: Used by realestate-brain/lib/claims.ts. A match is a flag for a human, not a legal finding.

claims.name: Guaranteed, assured or committed returns
claims.why: Promises of money can fall under deposit or investment-scheme laws and are a false guarantee under consumer law. The exact classification needs a lawyer.
claims.safer_wording: Describe the home and location. If the developer offers a rental arrangement, escalate to legal review before any mention.
claims.evidence_needed: Legal opinion on the specific arrangement.

claims.name: Price appreciation promises or projections
claims.why: Future prices are unknowable. A stated percentage reads as a promise and cannot be backed by the brochure.
claims.safer_wording: Say what has happened with a dated, sourced figure, or leave it out. Add no forecast.
claims.evidence_needed: A dated, named source for any historic figure, and no forward-looking number.

claims.name: Pre-launch, booking or offers before registration
claims.why: Advertising, marketing, booking or inviting purchase before registration is prohibited (s3(1)). Pre-launch language suggests that is exactly what is happening. If the project is registered, the wording may be fine.
claims.safer_wording: Confirm registration first. If registered, show the number and avoid booking-pressure language.
claims.evidence_needed: K-RERA registration number that matches this project and is not lapsed.

claims.name: 'RERA approved' or 'RERA certified'
claims.why: RERA registers projects. It does not approve plans or vouch for quality. 'Approved' can imply more than registration.
claims.safer_wording: RERA registered, with the registration number.

claims.name: Approval, khata, title or loan claims
claims.why: These are the claims buyers trust most, and the ones most costly if wrong. A brochure statement is not proof.
claims.safer_wording: Name the approval, the authority and the document number only when you hold the document. Example: 'RERA registered, number shown on screen.'
claims.evidence_needed: The document or portal record. 'RERA registered' needs the number to match the K-RERA record.

claims.name: Possession or handover dates
claims.why: The date declared at registration is binding. A different date in an ad is a false statement risk (s12) and feeds delay claims (s18).
claims.safer_wording: 'Registered completion date: [date as on the K-RERA record].' Never 'guaranteed' or 'will be ready'.
claims.evidence_needed: Completion date on the K-RERA project page.

claims.name: Price, EMI or 'starting at' claims
claims.why: Prices change and must match the verified source. 'No hidden charges' and 'all inclusive' are absolute claims that are easy to get wrong.
claims.safer_wording: Quote the number exactly as stated in the verified document, attributed to the developer. Drop absolutes.
claims.evidence_needed: Current price document and the developer's confirmation.

claims.name: Best, only, first, largest and 'no. 1' claims
claims.why: Comparative and absolute claims invite challenge and are rarely supported by the brochure.
claims.safer_wording: State the specific, checkable fact: '12-acre campus' or '480 apartments'.
claims.evidence_needed: A named, dated source in the brochure facts.

claims.name: Amenities and specifications
claims.why: Amenities must match the sanctioned plans, and renders are not proof. Only name what the brochure facts list, and confirm against the plan.
claims.safer_wording: Name amenities exactly as listed in the brochure facts.

claims.name: Distances, travel times and infrastructure
claims.why: Travel times vary by hour. Planned infrastructure is not infrastructure that exists.
claims.safer_wording: Use only verified locality facts with their source, and say 'planned' or 'proposed' where that is the status.
claims.evidence_needed: Verified entry in brain/localities.json with a source URL.

claims.name: Scarcity and deadline pressure
claims.why: Invented urgency pressures buyers into large decisions and is hard to prove.
claims.safer_wording: Only state a deadline the developer can document. Otherwise invite a site visit with no pressure.
claims.evidence_needed: Dated inventory or offer terms from the developer.

claims.name: Rental yield and income claims
claims.why: Income figures are forecasts, and implied certainty can slide into an assured-return claim.
claims.safer_wording: Skip it. If a historic local rent is used, cite a named, dated source and add no promise.
claims.evidence_needed: Named, dated source. Legal review if linked to the developer's own scheme.

claims.name: 'Subject to change' style disclaimers
claims.why: K-RERA told promoters not to use a disclaimer that the information is subject to change. Render and impression labels are not covered by that sentence; whether they are acceptable is a review question.
claims.safer_wording: Remove 'subject to change'. For renders, say 'render' plainly and escalate if unsure.

claims.name: Invented customers, testimonials and presenters
claims.why: An AI avatar cannot be a real buyer or resident, and customer numbers need proof.
claims.safer_wording: Remove, or use only a real, consented testimonial supplied by the developer with a record of consent.
claims.evidence_needed: Written consent and the original testimonial.

claims.name: Legal or financial advice stated as fact
claims.why: RealBrain is not a licensed advisor. Never tell buyers to skip checks.
claims.safer_wording: 'Check the registration on the K-RERA website before you decide.'

claims.name: Tell buyers to verify the registration
claims.why: Encourages the check the law is designed around.
claims.safer_wording: 'Search the registration number on rera.karnataka.gov.in before you pay anything.'

claims.name: General RERA protections for buyers
claims.why: True by statute. Say 'RERA requires'. Do not claim this specific developer complies, and say it only about registered projects.
claims.safer_wording: 'Under RERA, a developer cannot take more than 10% as an advance before a registered agreement for sale.'

advertisement_checklist.item: RERA registration number on screen, top right, whole video, large enough to read (at least half the project-name text size, as the print rule says)
Number also in the caption, copied exactly from the verified record
www.rera.karnataka.gov.in on screen and in the caption
Every number matches the verified facts
No dates promised; any date equals the registered completion date
No returns, appreciation, urgency or superlative claims without a source
Approval claims backed by a document
'AI-generated' label visible for the whole video; no avatar posed as a real buyer or the founder
Developer approves the final script and video (the developer is liable for the claims)

when: A rule's status is not verified_primary and the script depends on it
Two sources disagree (for example the 500 sq m / 8 apartments test)
A claim class is 'conditional' and the evidence is missing
A rental, buy-back or assured-income arrangement is mentioned
The developer asks to use a disclaimer, a QR code or a placement different from the checklist
The publisher is a broker or channel partner rather than the promoter
how: 1. RealBrain stops approval for that script and shows a plain message: what is unclear and why.
2. It creates an escalation record: script id, rule id, the exact question (the rule's escalation_question), the text in question, sources already checked, date.
3. A human (the developer's legal advisor, or the founder for RealBrain's own rules) answers in writing.
4. The answer is saved with the date. Only then may a rule's status change, and only by a human edit to compliance_rules.json.
5. RealBrain never marks anything verified, never decides a legal question, and never publishes on its own.
escalation.storage: Not built yet. When Stage 4 adds a data store, escalation records belong there, not in git.
